Diagnostic Services

Comprehensive Diagnostic Services at Embryogenesis

EmbryoGenesis, an infertility diagnostic and research centre in Mohali, Punjab, offers three endometrial tests: ERFA – The Soil Test, the Endo-Immune Test and the Endometrial Infection Test (EIT).

At Embryogenesis, we know that understanding the root cause of fertility challenges is the first step toward successful treatment. Our state-of-the-art diagnostic services are designed to provide detailed insights into reproductive health, enabling personalized and effective care for individuals and couples seeking answers.

Test 1

Endometrial Receptivity & Function Assay (ERFA – The Soil Test)

What is ERFA – The Soil Test?

The ERFA, or Endometrial Soil Test, is a groundbreaking diagnostic tool that assesses the readiness of the uterine lining (endometrium) for successful embryo implantation. This comprehensive test analyzes multiple biomarkers to pinpoint factors affecting fertility and implantation success.

Who is ERFA for?

  • Individuals with unexplained infertility
  • Those who have experienced recurrent implantation failure (RIF)
  • Women facing repeated IVF failures or recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL); see IVF फेलियर के बाद गर्भावस्था के लिए आवश्यक उपाय और उपचार (Hindi)

What are the benefits of ERFA?

  • Provides a full profile of endometrial receptivity
  • Explains hidden causes of implantation challenges
  • Guides personalized treatment strategies

“Gain crucial insights into your fertility journey with ERFA – The Soil Test.”

When is the ERFA sample taken, and how soon are results ready?

ERFA – The Soil Test needs an endometrial tissue biopsy, collected by curettage (D&C) or needle biopsy, on menstrual cycle day 21–23 (preferably the 21st day), on LH+7 to LH+9 in a natural cycle, or on P+6 to P+8 in an HRT / mock cycle. Results are typically available within 7–10 days, depending on the complexity of the test.

Test 2

Endo-Immune Test

What is the Endo-Immune Test?

This test delves into the immune landscape of the endometrium, essential for maintaining a balance between pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory responses. By evaluating cytokines and immune cells, we help identify potential immune-related issues causing recurrent miscarriages or failed implantation.

Key highlights of the Endo-Immune Test

  • Assesses immune competency to support healthy embryo implantation
  • Identifies imbalances in cytokine levels and uNK cell activity
  • Offers targeted insights for immune-modulatory treatments

“Find answers to immune-related fertility challenges and explore tailored solutions.”

Read more: Endometrial Immune Profiling: What It Is, Why It Matters, and Who Should Consider It

Test 3

Endometrial Infection Test (EIT)

What is the Endometrial Infection Test (EIT)?

Endometrial infections can go unnoticed but may severely impact fertility by altering the environment needed for successful implantation. The Endometrial Infection Test detects hidden bacterial or viral infections and chronic endometritis.

Who should consider the Endometrial Infection Test?

  • Women with recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL)
  • Those experiencing repeated IVF failures or unexplained infertility

Advantages of the EIT

  • Detects asymptomatic infections affecting fertility
  • Ensures a thorough assessment for a healthier endometrial environment

“Ensure your endometrium is prepared for a healthy pregnancy with our EIT.”

FAQs

What can I expect during these diagnostic tests?

Each test includes a comprehensive consultation, a simple collection process, and a detailed explanation of results. Our specialists ensure you feel informed and supported throughout.

How soon will I get my results?

Results are typically available within 7-10 days, depending on the complexity of the test. We prioritize accuracy and timely reporting to help you move forward confidently.

Will these tests help if I’ve already had IVF treatments?

Absolutely. Our diagnostic tests are particularly beneficial for those who have faced IVF failures or unexplained fertility issues. They provide deeper insights that standard tests may miss.

Information only. Testing is ordered and interpreted by your treating doctor.
